title: 这, 那, 哪 (+些): this, that, which
summary: Lets you point to things near and far, one or many, and ask which one, as in 这个, 那些 and 哪些.
structure: 这 / 那 / 哪 + (Number) + Measure word + Noun
这些 / 那些 / 哪些 + Noun
explanation:
这 means "this" (near you), 那 means "that" (farther away), and 哪 means "which?" and is used to ask questions. Add 些 and they become plural: 这些 "these", 那些 "those", 哪些 "which ones?".

Before a noun, 这, 那 and 哪 normally need a measure word (a small counting word like 个, 本, 件): 这个人 "this person", 那本书 "that book", 哪件衣服 "which piece of clothing?". To add a number, put it right after 这 / 那 / 哪: 这三本书 "these three books". With 些, you don't need a measure word: 这些书, 那些人.

On their own, 这 and 那 can be the subject of a 是 sentence: 这是我的手机 "This is my phone." 这个, 那个, 这些 and 那些 can also stand alone when the thing is clear: 那些很贵 "Those are expensive."

Watch out: 那 (that) and 哪 (which) look alike. 哪 has the 口 "mouth" part on the left, because it asks something. Since 哪 already makes a question, don't add 吗. Also, don't mix 些 with a number: say 这三本书, not 这些三本书.

examples.zh: 这些苹果很便宜，那些很贵。
examples.en: These apples are cheap; those are expensive.

examples.zh: 桌子上的书，哪些是你的？
examples.en: Which of the books on the table are yours?

mistakes.why: Before a noun, 那 needs a measure word. For clothes, use 件.
With a number, use 这 + number + measure word. 些 already means "several", so it doesn't go with a number.
哪 already makes the sentence a question, so you don't add 吗.

exercises.en: I want to buy that piece of clothing.
why: Correct: 那 + measure word 件 + noun means "that piece of clothing".
那些 is plural and replaces the measure word, so it can't be followed by 件.
哪 means "which" and makes a question, but this sentence is a statement about "that" one.
那个 already has a measure word (个), so you can't add 件 too. Use only one measure word.
Correct: 哪 + 本 + 书 asks "which book?".
那 means "that", not "which". 那 and 哪 look alike, but only 哪 asks a question.
这些 means "these" and replaces the measure word, so it can't come before 本. It also doesn't ask a question.
什么 means "what" and goes straight before a noun (什么书). It doesn't take a measure word like 本.
Correct: 这些 + noun means "these", with no measure word needed.
Don't put 个 between 这 and 些. 这些 is one word.
些 can't be used alone here. It needs 这 or 那 in front to mean "these" or "those".
哪些 means "which ones?" and makes a question, but this sentence is a statement.

exercises.prompt: Which means 'Which students are coming tomorrow?'
why: Correct: 哪些 + noun asks "which ones?" about more than one person.
那些 means "those", so this says "Those students are coming tomorrow." It's not a question.
哪些 already makes a question, so you don't add 吗.
Don't put 个 inside 哪些. Use 哪个 for one and 哪些 for more than one.
Correct: 这 + number + measure word + noun, as in 这两本书.
Don't use 些 with a number. Say 这两本书.
这 comes first, then the number: 这两本书, not 两这本书.
A measure word is needed after the number: 两本书, not 两书.
Correct: replace 这 with 哪 in the same spot, and the sentence becomes a question.
哪 already makes a question, so 吗 is not needed.
那 means "that", not "which". This only asks "You want that one?"
哪 and 个 stay together in the object's position: 你要哪个？
Correct: 这些 replaces 这 + measure word, giving 这些书.
With 些 you drop the measure word, so 本 must go.
们 isn't added to things like 书. Use 这些 for the plural.
The order is 这些, not 些这.

exercises.why: 那 is the subject before 是, and the owner (我老师的) comes before the thing owned.
哪些 + noun sits where the answer would go, here after the verb 要, just like 这些苹果 would.

exercises.en: Those three people are my friends.
exercises.why: The order is 那 + number + measure word + noun: 那三个人.
